title: Hotfix: tenant route throttle caused cross-region model swap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production incident caused by a route-evaluation throttle interaction resulted in requests from a small set of enterprise tenants being routed to an incompatible, low-cost regional model variant (quantized and different region) instead of their pinned Dedicated variant. Customer reports: increased latency variability and incorrect generation quality. This ticket documents the hotfix, the root cause, verification, and follow-ups.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-25T13:02 and 2026-02-25T14:18 UTC, ~0.3% of requests for 6 enterprise tenants were silently routed to an incompatible regional model variant. Customers observed degraded output quality and transient compliance flagging. Pager escalations from 2 customers, one support SLA breach logged.
root_cause: A recently deployed protection that rate-limited route-evaluation jobs under high config churn introduced a 600ms evaluation delay for tenant-affinity checks. The delayed policy snapshot expired and the fallback evaluator used a stale global fallback order that preferred a cost-optimized regional variant. The sequence: (1) throttle applied to policy-eval workers during config churn, (2) evaluator skipped tenant-scoped priority checks due to stale TTL, (3) fallback comparator selected wrong variant because comparator tie-breaker fell back to lexicographic region ID instead of explicit tier policy.
mitigation_and_hotfix:
- Hotfix deployed 2026-02-25T14:03 UTC: reverted the policy-eval throttle flag and reinstated synchronous tenant-affinity checks for requests hitting enterprise profiles.
- Emergency change to fallback comparator to prefer explicit tier attribute over lexicographic region ID.
- Short-term rollback of the throttle feature to avoid delaying policy snapshots.
- Customer-targeted cache invalidation triggered for affected tenants.
timeline:
- 2026-02-25 13:00 UTC: config churn from onboarding job triggered policy-eval backlog.
- 2026-02-25 13:08 UTC: Monitoring alert: increased fallback rate for region-eu and model-compat mismatches.
- 2026-02-25 13:15 UTC: Customer support received first escalations.

- 2026-02-25 14:18 UTC: Metrics returned to baseline.

- 2026-03-10: Rollout completed to all regions; ticket closed.
reproduction_steps:
1) Create tenant with pinned dedicated variant (example tenant ID used internally).
2) Introduce synthetic config churn to enqueue policy snapshot updates.
3) Enable policy-eval throttle flag to simulate 600ms evaluation delay.
4) Send traffic matching affinity filter; observe evaluated fallback path in logs and compare to expected tenant-scoped variant.
5) Confirm comparator tie-break observed lexicographic region preference instead of tier attribute.
Note: reproduction requires config flags and internal tenant fixtures; do not run against production tenants.
acceptance_criteria:
- No tenant experiences routing to an incompatible regional model variant in canary for 24h.
- Policy-eval latency under synthetic churn is <100ms for enterprise-class tenants.
- Comparator unit tests cover tie-break behavior and prefer tier attribute over region ID.
- Rollout to prod completed with dashboards showing fallback-rate <0.01% of requests for 7 days.
post_deployment_tests:
- End-to-end checks sending requests to 10 tenant fixtures across regions, validate model variant returned matches pinned variant.
- Load test with controlled config churn to ensure snapshot pipeline recovers within 200ms.
- Smoke test for Dedicated customers to verify isolation and no silent downgrade.
follow_up_tasks:
- RFC: proposal to add tenant-affinity health signals to the routing decision path (owner: Luca).
- Implement a prioritized comparator rewrite with explicit weighting and comprehensive tests (owner: Routing team).
- Add telemetry: expose policy-eval latency per tenant and fallback rationale in audit logs.
- Run a chaos exercise to simulate config churn and verify routing invariants.
- Customer outreach: send incident summary and remediation notes to affected customers with credits applied (owner: CS/SE).
